turns.assessment: The ~4.5 dB change is confined to the S17 receiver side of och54: upstream channel monitors and every amplifier on the S10–S19–S18–S17 path remained stable, while all affected services share this lightpath. This strongly localizes the fault after the S17 ingress monitor, most plausibly to per-channel WSS attenuation at S17. The later small excursion on the unrelated S21–S19 input is not temporally or topologically consistent with the main event.

proposals.rationale: A per-channel attenuation drift in the S17 ROADM can lower och54 power between the stable ingress OCM and trx.och54.z, affecting every service carried by och54 without changing other channels or upstream amplifier telemetry.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A receiver-local defect could produce anomalous local power and estimated-OSNR readings while the optical path remains normal, but the absence of pre-FEC BER degradation makes this less consistent than actual local attenuation.
A dirty local optical connection could introduce loss after the ingress monitor, but the documented OMS-input failure should normally affect all channels rather than only och54.
